raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The `resize with live allocations` subtest in `test_unified_post_capture_sizing.py` finalizes a 64 MiB reservation to 16 MiB, then allocates before resizing the allocator. The full-attention allocator still grows down from the old 64 MiB frontier, so allocation-time `_zero_pages_kernel` writes into the unbacked tail instead of reaching the intended `non-empty` assertion.

Observed in [this CI failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38988923342/job/117270212489): `CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_MMU_FAULT` in `_zero_pages_kernel`, process exit code -6. The affected test and allocator code are also present on main; this is independent of #43387.

## Modifications

Resize the empty allocator immediately after finalizing backing, before creating the live allocation. The subsequent resize still verifies that a non-empty allocator is rejected. This matches the production startup ordering and changes only the test setup.

## Validation

- Python syntax and `git diff --check` passed.
- Pre-commit checks run on the changed file.
- CUDA execution is pending CI; the local machine has no NVIDIA GPU. The diagnosis is based on the failing CI log and the allocation/backing code path.

Targeted GPU command:

```bash
python test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_post_capture_sizing.py
```

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: test-only change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: test-only change.

files.patch:
@@ -180,6 +180,9 @@ def test_sizing_contract_is_enforced(self):
             kvcache.finalize_backing(
                 SimpleNamespace(unified_memory_pool_bytes=_FINAL_BYTES)
             )
+            # Move the grow-down allocator's frontier into the backed range
+            # before allocating; it still reflects the larger reservation.
+            allocator.resize(SimpleNamespace(unified_memory_pool_bytes=_FINAL_BYTES))
             handed = allocator.alloc(_PAGE_SIZE)
             self.assertIsNotNone(handed)
             with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "non-empty"):
